prediction: #433, addendum 2 of the brief: where the race start's period goes once the report wait is gone. A is today's default code with the frametrace on; B adds HAKUX_REPORT_ASYNC=1 (the report fence leaves the PFIFO thread) and HAKUX_TEXSCAN=1 (the cube-face/range-scan sd finishes go). Both perflog, so CPU rows carry the perflog cost (~0.8 plain/perflog, nfs30plan1010 NOTES 5.5) and waits do not. Predicted at the warm countdown: F: the report fence on the PFIFO thread (p_c_rep, waits under pgraph_process_pending_reports) is >= 2.5 ms/frame on A and <= 0.5 on B. U: the PFIFO thread's blocked time at no hooked site (the sd finishes' finish_event wait) falls by >= 4 ms/frame A -> B (A ~10, B ~1-3: what is left is wait_frame_submitted and the rule-3 gate). P: the frame period B - A <= -2.5 ms (point -4; the plain-build pair measured -3.5, and quantization to the VBLANK grid keeps it far below the ~14 ms of waits removed). R: on B, the PFIFO thread's on-CPU time (p_run) is >= 50 % of the period, i.e. the residual is CPU work on the pacing thread, not a wait: recording (phase Draw) is its largest named part, pidle (waiting for the guest's next frame, the VBLANK grid) the second-largest row, the report fence ~0, other hooked fences <= 1 ms, cube faces (unhooked) <= 3 ms. What refutes it: F or U failing with the [reportasync] on line and texscan's [tsc] route present (a wait moved to another PFIFO site, which p_oth_hk or unhooked would show); R failing (the residual is a wait, which its row names). The reader thread's own fence waits land in o_fence (unregistered thread) on B and are not on the pacing thread.
